story.title: Selma Blair Apologizes Following Plane Incident and Arrest
story.summary: Selma Blair has publicly apologized for her behavior following an incident on a plane earlier this month, during which she was arrested for alleged assault. This marks her first public remarks since the event.

explore_lenses.label: What does Blair’s apology address?
explore_lenses.title: Apology acknowledges harm, not guilt
explore_lenses.summary: Blair’s first public video apology focuses on people she says she hurt, frightened or alarmed. It does not change her not-guilty plea or resolve the allegations now before state and potentially federal authorities.

claims.text: Blair said she was sorry to people she had disappointed, hurt, frightened or alarmed, while saying she had never intended to hurt or frighten anyone.
She has pleaded not guilty to two New York second-degree assault counts tied to alleged conduct involving a Port Authority officer and a hospital nurse after the flight.
Her representatives contend that she experienced a medical emergency and did not intend to harm anyone; that is their account, not a court finding.

Her representatives contend that she experienced a medical emergency and did not intend to harm anyone; that is their account, not a court finding.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The apology does not specify what caused the incident or concede the alleged assaults.

explore_lenses.label: What is alleged to have happened on the trip?
explore_lenses.title: Separate flight and post-landing allegations
explore_lenses.summary: The reported episode has two legal components: alleged injuries to flight attendants during the Los Angeles-to-JFK flight, and state charges based on alleged assaults after landing. Keeping those allegations distinct matters because they are being handled through different processes.

claims.text: Port Authority police said they responded to a report of a physically abusive passenger on Delta Flight 938; two flight attendants reported injuries and one was taken to a hospital for evaluation.
The Queens criminal complaint alleges Blair kicked a Port Authority officer while being secured to a stretcher and later kicked a registered nurse at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center.
Blair’s representatives dispute reports that she tried to open an aircraft door and say her neurological conditions and a medical emergency are relevant context.

Blair’s representatives dispute reports that she tried to open an aircraft door and say her neurological conditions and a medical emergency are relevant context.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the criminal cases?
explore_lenses.title: A January state court date; federal path unclear
explore_lenses.summary: The New York state case has been adjourned to January, while an assault matter related to conduct aboard the aircraft remains on a separate federal track. Neither process has produced a judgment.

claims.text: The state case was adjourned until January 19, according to the Queens district attorney’s office as reported by NBC News.

The FBI issued Blair a federal violation notice alleging assault within federal special maritime and territorial jurisdiction; AP reported that matter would proceed in Brooklyn federal petty-violations court, with no appearance date then set.
Whether either case results in dismissal, a plea agreement or trial cannot yet be determined from the public record.

story_report.summary: Selma Blair has issued her first public remarks since her arrest after an incident on a plane, apologizing to people she said she may have disappointed, hurt, frightened or alarmed. She said she never intended to hurt or frighten anyone. Blair was charged with assault following the episode and has pleaded not guilty to two New York second-degree assault counts tied to alleged conduct after the flight.

sections.heading: Flight Reports and Assault Allegations
sections.body: Port Authority police said they responded to a report of a physically abusive passenger on Delta Flight 938. Two flight attendants reported injuries, and one was taken to a hospital for evaluation, according to police. A Queens criminal complaint alleges Blair kicked a Port Authority officer while she was being secured to a stretcher and later kicked a registered nurse at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center; those allegations have not been adjudicated.

sections.heading: Blair Representatives Cite Medical Emergency
sections.body: Blair’s representatives say she experienced a medical emergency and did not intend to harm anyone, an account that is not a court finding. They also dispute reports that she tried to open an aircraft door and say her neurological conditions are relevant context. Blair’s apology did not specify what caused the incident or concede the alleged assaults.

sections.heading: State and Federal Cases Remain Pending
sections.body: The Queens district attorney’s office said the state case was adjourned until Jan. 19, according to NBC News. Separately, the FBI issued Blair a federal violation notice alleging assault within federal special maritime and territorial jurisdiction; the Associated Press reported the matter would proceed in Brooklyn federal petty-violations court. No federal appearance date had been publicly reported as of Oct. 31, 2026.

unresolved.text: Public reporting does not establish a final medical explanation for the episode.
The public record does not determine whether either case will end in dismissal, a plea agreement or trial.

related_stories.title: BJP Criticizes Opposition's Mock Parliament and Challenges Gandhi to Debate
related_stories.summary: The BJP has criticized the opposition's mock Parliament initiative, with MP Sambit Patra suggesting that Rahul Gandhi should be made a 'mock PM.' Patra dismissed the opposition's allegations of electoral fraud, citing that similar events occurred during Congress rule. Additionally, Home Minister Amit Shah has challenged Gandhi to debate the allegations of vote theft in Parliament, coinciding with an upcoming opposition rally in Delhi.

related_stories.title: UK Prime Minister Open to Slavery Apology Amid Caribbean Tour
related_stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has expressed openness to a formal apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade. This statement comes as King Charles continues his tour of the Caribbean, where discussions about the UK's colonial history are prominent. However, Burnham has ruled out the possibility of financial reparations, despite ongoing demands from Caribbean nations.
